classification.difficultyReason: Use the wire-length constraint to express two square areas in one variable and simplify the resulting quadratic.

content.prompt: A 30 cm length of wire is cut into 2 pieces and each piece bent to form a square as shown.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8, figure beneath parts a and b
spec.description: One horizontal wire with endpoint ticks and an interior cut tick. Its left portion is labelled x and right portion y; 30 cm labels the complete wire. A larger square appears beneath the left portion and a smaller square beneath the right. No square side lengths are supplied.
spec.mathematics: The two wire portions have lengths x and y with x+y=30; each portion forms the perimeter of its respective square. The figure is schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question figure; no calculated side lengths or areas are shown.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the total area of the 2 squares is given by $A=\dfrac{x^2-30x+450}{8}$.

answer.worked:
The perimeter of one square is $x$, so its side is $\dfrac{x}{4}$. The other square has side $\dfrac{y}{4}$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)^2+\left(\frac{y}{4}\right)^2\\A&=\frac{x^2+y^2}{16}\\A&=\frac{x^2+(30-x)^2}{16}\\A&=\frac{900-60x+2x^2}{16}\\A&=\frac{x^2-30x+450}{8}\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
